BPH is common in older men and occurs due to the expansion of transitional epithelium. This can lead to obstruction of the urethra causing difficulty when urinating. The prostate surrounds the urethra as it passes through the center of the prostate gland. The urethra passes through the transition zone which lies between 15-30mm from the external urethral sphincter. The transition zone is therefore the most common location for enlargement to occur as it is the narrowest point of the urethra. The anterior fibromuscular stroma is found at the periphery of the gland and surrounds the prostatic ducts. The central zone is made up of dense irregular connective tissue. The oblique zones are located on either side of the prostate and contain both glands and ducts. The periphery is similar to the anterior stroma except the ducts open directly into the prostatic sinuses. B is the correct answer!Nociception- painExteroception- touchInteroception- sensing viscera movementKinesthesis- muscle and joint position/movement proprioception is carried via articular nerves and is the sense of the position and motion of the body parts. It allows us to maintain equilibrium and posture. This is why when the nerve of a joint is damaged it causes loss of proprioception. The reason behind hilton's law is that if the nerve to the joint is damaged then the muscles cannot be contracted and therefore will not pull on the bones to move the joint. This was discovered by a doctor called Charles Hilton who studied reflexes in frogs. He found that if he cut the nerve to a muscle, the frog could no longer extend its leg but if he cut the nerve to the joint, the frog could still extend its leg. He concluded that the nerves supplied the muscle did not carry motor impulses to the muscle and that they must travel along with the nerve to the joint.He then went on to discover that the same nerve innervated both the muscle and the joint, so the nerve of the joint also carried motor impulses to the muscles. He called this law of nerve innervation "Hilton's Law". This can also be applied to the skin. If the nerve of a joint is damaged then the patient may experience clumsiness as they are unable to feel where their limbs are and what they are doing. This is because the proprioceptive information from the muscles and joints is missing (proprioceptors are mechanoreceptors that detect changes in position, length and load of the associated muscles). The proprioceptive information helps to adjust stance and gait. http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/20379845 http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Scott_Sherrington#cite_note-14-14 http://teachmeanatomy.info/lower-limb/joints/knee-joint/innervation/ https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/biochemistry-genetics-and-molecular-biology/nociception http://teachmeanatom
